name: Input buffering for attacks
summary: A press made during an attack's recovery is saved and fires the moment the attack ends, instead of being thrown away.
what_it_does: Players press the next attack before the current one finishes. If the game only accepts input when the character is idle, those presses vanish and combat feels sticky. A buffer keeps one press made near the end of recovery and starts the next attack on the first frame it's allowed.
use_when: Melee combat, combos, fighting games, any move with recovery time.
watch_out: Keep it to one queued press. Queueing every press makes the character keep swinging after the player stopped.
starting_values: A buffer of 100 to 200 ms before recovery ends. Recovery itself of 150 to 300 ms for a light attack.
prompt:
Add an input buffer for attacks.
- Each attack has an active phase and a recovery phase (220 ms).
- If attack is pressed while an attack is running and less than 150 ms of it remain, queue one press.
- When recovery ends and a press is queued, start the next attack on that frame.
- Earlier presses are ignored. Only one press can be queued.
- Show a debug counter of dropped presses.

Acceptance checks:
1. Pressing attack again 75 ms before recovery ends chains into a second attack with no idle frame.
2. Pressing attack at the very start of an attack does not queue anything.
3. Holding the button does not auto-attack.
